pl-l2d29c3-d1e108.summary: States that in punishment of sin man was cast out of paradise into this place of miseries, lest he put out his hand, take from the tree of life, and live forever (Gen 3:22–23); this seems to suggest he would never die if he later ate from it.
claims: Expulsion was a punishment of sin.

pl-l2d29c3.summary: States that as punishment for that sin man was expelled from paradise into this place of miseries (Gen 3:22–23), lest he take from the tree of life and live forever; the words seem to suggest he would never have died had he afterward eaten from it.
claims: Man was expelled from paradise as punishment for sin.
Genesis seems to say he would have lived forever had he eaten from the tree of life after sin.
